thread:
maria: quick heads-up — bringing raptor-int8 into the canary pool. seeing intermittent funcall JSON parse failures in streaming mode, usually ~2-5% of requests :thinking_face:

maria: example of one failing stream (truncated/extra tokens):
```
...
"tools": [{"name": "lookup", "args": {"id": 123}}],
}
```

devon: can you paste the raw model output chunk that produced that? streaming boundary or tokenization issue?

maria: pasted below — boundary cut inside closing brace, looks like `...}]},"extra` then stream closed. occurs more when requests have long kv-prefixes.

sanjay: suspect interaction of kv-cache and quantization noise. int8 seems to occasionally shift tokenization probabilities so EOS gets emitted mid-structure. also seen when temp>0.5.

lina: i ran a small sample-based eval: 1000 prompts, 5 samples per prompt, soft-schema acceptance (allow missing trailing commas) and a merge heuristic that picks longest valid JSON. quick numbers: success@1=0.41, success@3=0.69, success@5=0.82, repair-by-merge=0.12. attaching harness output summary.

maria: thanks. i prototyped a "stochastic repair" flow: sample N completions (N=3), attempt parse each, if any valid -> return; if none valid, try merge heuristic + minimal fixes (quote balance, trailing comma removal). reduces hard failures but adds ~80-120ms p50.

devon: what's retry policy today? we have retry_budget=1 for hosted. can we make it adaptive: if parse fails and model is canary -> allow 2 retries with temp ramp?

maria: proposal: retry_budget=2, temp schedule: [0.2, 0.45, 0.7] across original+2 retries, top_p fixed 0.95, abort if total latency>700ms. also short-circuit if parse_confidence>0.8 on first try.

sanjay: +1 but watch throughput. retries will amplify quota. maybe only enable for routes with low qps or for dedicated. we can gate by cost tier.

lina: added a parse-confidence metric to the eval harness (soft score from tokenizer-prob mass around bracket tokens). baseline: avg_parse_confidence: 0.62 for failures, 0.85 for clean responses. threshold 0.75 seems to separate nicely.

maria: sample command i used for the harness:
```
./eval_canary \
  --model raptor-int8 \
  --prompts-file prompts/devex.jsonl \
  --samples 5 \
  --merge-mode stochastic \
  --parse-threshold 0.75 \
  --save=results/raptor_int8_samples.jsonl
```

eval-bot: quick digest from run #2026-03-19T14:22Z:
- total prompts: 1000
- success@1: 0.41
- success@3: 0.69
- success@5: 0.82
- avg latency baseline: 220ms -> +95ms with merge flow
- estimated extra token cost @scale: +11%

devon: rough action items: 1) enable retry-budget=2 behind canary flag + telemetry; 2) add parse_confidence metric to API response headers; 3) run 10k-prompt eval comparing merge vs retry ramp cost/quality curves.

maria: i'm taking 1 & 2. i'll add a per-route gate so we don't blast free-tier traffic.

sanjay: i'll simulate server-side kv-cache interleaving to try reproduce deterministic failure; also will run a tokenization-prob trace to see if EOS probability spikes mid-structure.

lina: i'll scale the sample harness to 10k prompts and include a small human-reviewed label set (200) to measure semantic correctness after repair. want to know if merge introduces hallucinated fields.

ops-bot: deploy(v0.78.3-canary) scheduled to canary pool at 2026-03-20T03:00Z :eyes:

maria: one more thing — consider lightweight client-side sanitizer that rejects obviously truncated chunks and triggers immediate retry before merge. cheaper than sampling more.

devon: agree. add client-side quick-parse check + immediate 1 retry with temp=0.6. if still bad -> fall back to server merge flow.

maria: ok created PR with a small implementation and telemetry hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3347 :thumbsup:

lina: will run the expanded eval tomorrow and post results in this thread. if we see merge causing semantic drift we'll fail the canary.

maria: thanks all — let's sync after the 10k run. :rocket:
